evidence: src/enrolments/enrolments.controller.ts: enrol() reads courseId and studentEmail from the DTO and passes them to enrolmentsService.enrol, which is plain delegation.
src/enrolments/enrolments.controller.ts: withdraw() calls enrolmentsService.withdraw and wraps the result as { refund }, which is only response shaping (a presentation concern).
Routing uses only NestJS decorators (@Controller('enrolments'), @Post(), @Post('withdrawals'), @Body()), which is a transport concern that belongs in presentation.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The controller does only presentation work. It sets up HTTP routes with NestJS decorators (@Controller, @Post, @Body), reads fields from the request DTO, hands the work to EnrolmentsService, and shapes the response (wrapping the refund boolean in an object). It contains no business rules, no persistence and no domain logic. The decision about whether a refund is owed happens in the service, not here.
